page_title: Implementing Real-time Object Detection System using PyTorch and OpenCV

summary.title: Implementing Real-time Object Detection System using PyTorch and OpenCV
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simple real-time object detection prototype in Python by reading a video stream, scoring frames with YOLOv5 loaded from PyTorch Hub, drawing boxes with OpenCV, and writing the output stream.
keywords: how to build object detection prototype
python vs c++ for real-time vision
takeaways: Video input can come from a YouTube URL, a local webcam, or an IP camera, all read through OpenCV.
YOLOv5 is chosen for fast inference; it can be loaded directly from PyTorch Hub and is cached on disk after the first download.
Each frame is scored by the model, boxes are plotted with OpenCV, and the processed frame is written to an output stream in a loop.
A GPU with CUDA is said to substantially raise throughput (about 45-60 FPS reported versus 25-30 FPS on CPU, per the author's experience).
The author argues Python is acceptable for a prototype because heavy work runs in C++ inside PyTorch and OpenCV, but is not ideal for production real-time systems.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a prototype real-time object detection application in Python. It covers reading video from YouTube, a webcam, or an IP camera with OpenCV, loading the YOLOv5 model from PyTorch Hub, scoring single frames, and plotting labelled boxes over detections. The pieces are combined into one looped function (read frame, score, plot, write) that the author suggests packaging into a class. The author notes that performance depends on hardware, with GPUs giving much higher frame rates than CPUs, and points to the full code on GitHub.
